engines.name: Surface-hop compiler (time-window intersection, density refusal, rejected-hop log)
engines.one_line: Derives actor-to-actor hops only from shared hop-eligible bounded surfaces; hop window = intersection of surface window and both participation windows (year/month/day widened to full period); refuses surfaces over max_hop_actor_count (19) and broad-institution-only surfaces; records refused surfaces and non-overlapping pairs; BFS shortest path with as-of slicing and a dated/partially_dated/surface_window_only/undated basis status.
engines.inputs: surfaces[] (hop_eligible, time_start/time_end, receipt_ids), participation rows (actor|organization, time_start/time_end, evidence_class, receipt_ids), receipts by id, set of broad-organization ids, density policy {max_hop_actor_count}
engines.outputs: edges[] each with per-surface bases (valid_from/valid_until, temporal_status, weakest evidence class, roles, receipts); rejected_hop_surfaces[] (reason enum); rejected_hop_pairs[] (windows, receipts, reverifiable flag, publication_status); adjacency; shortestPath(asOf)
engines.coupling_notes: Library files are plain ESM, zero npm deps; evidence vocabulary (official, primary_public, reported, derived, judgment, open) is hard-coded in ledger.mjs. build-hop-graph.mjs hard-codes ANCHOR_ACTOR_ID matt-clifford, reads legacy graph.json, cases.json default_case_id and data/intake/defense-industrial-candidates.json, and writes five build/*.json files.

tests.note: temporal/density/hop-stints use synthetic inline fixtures, i.e. portable as-is. The rejected-pair path is exercised only by fixtures and validate-release: the live ledger yields 93 edges, 35 rejected surfaces and 0 rejected pairs.

engines.lift_out: Copy hops.mjs + temporal.mjs + density.mjs (~400 LOC) and inline the three ledger.mjs helpers; parameterise the evidence-class table and broad-org set; write a 30-line driver. About half a day. Port tests/temporal, density, hop-stints verbatim.

engines.name: Hop query CLI and route projections (6 route modes, diagnostics)
engines.one_line: CLI `--from X [--to Y] [--as-of YYYY[-MM[-DD]]] [--json]` prints the shortest evidenced path with per-hop shared surfaces and windows; the browser-safe route-projections module adds shortest (canonical), strongest-evidence, best-dated, official-only, as-of and blocked-segments projections, all secondary and never changing a hop count.
engines.inputs: build/hop-graph.json (edges + rejected_hop_pairs), build/axm-identity.json for id aliasing
engines.outputs: text or JSON path {number, actor_path, hops[]}; projection objects tagged kind clifford|secondary
engines.coupling: low (route-projections, evidence-rank, route-diagnostics: pure ESM, only import evidence-rank) / medium (query-hops: needs two build files and the identity layer)

tests.note: No standalone test of the CLI flag parsing; route-projections.test.js spawns it.

engines.lift_out: Copy the four src/ modules unchanged (<1k LOC, browser + node). Re-implement the 76-line CLI against your own graph path. A few hours.

engines.name: Receipt archiving gate (SHA-256 content hash or Wayback ref) with limits text
engines.one_line: Every receipt row must carry archive.method in_repo_content_hash (sha256:<64hex> of the repo-relative extract, CRLF-normalised for text types, path-escape and symlink checks) or internet_archive (timestamped web.archive.org URL whose target equals one of the receipt's source URLs); unrecoverable_local_paste is a failure; enforcement date 2027-01-01 unless strict.
engines.inputs: receipt rows {receipt_id, path, source_url, archive:{method, ref, captured, checked}}
engines.coupling_notes: Only imports `root` from ledger.mjs. Offline: it never fetches the Wayback snapshot, only checks the URL shape.
caveats: The SHA-256 covers the project's own paraphrased extract (68 of 73 receipts use in_repo_content_hash on a repo extract: 57 in receipts/topology, 11 in receipts/thesis-state-market), not the upstream page; only 5 receipts have a Wayback snapshot. It is tamper-evidence for the extract, not proof the source says it.

The "limits" text is convention, not code: 38 of 57 receipt files have a Limits / Adjudication boundary / Boundary heading, 19 do not, and no validator or test greps for it. Every receipt row has a `notes` field (73/73).
engines.lift_out: Copy the file (it is self-contained) and the receipt row convention; add a check that requires a limits heading if you want the "limits" rule enforced. ~2 hours.

engines.name: Narrator that adds no facts (plain blocks, machine-derived fallback)

engines.lift_out: narration.mjs is 28 lines and portable; narrate-hops.mjs needs the actor registry shape. ~half a day.

engines.name: FEC x OGE payee/entity name matcher + temporal screen
engines.one_line: Streaming three-rule candidate generator: exact normalised name; conservative base/parenthetical forms; token-indexed high similarity (>=2 shared distinctive tokens, Jaccard>=0.75 or subset containment+dice>=0.8, posting-list cap 2% and >=250). Temporal screen can only prove NON-overlap from disjoint bounds; aggregate FEC ranges never establish overlap.
engines.inputs: JSONL of OGE interests, JSONL of FEC payee candidates
engines.outputs: overlap candidates + rejection examples + manifest (all graph_effect none)
engines.live_result: 5,945 OGE interests x 46,926 FEC payees (278.8M naive pairs not materialised) -> 1,172 candidate pairs touching 221 interests; 88 exact-name rows examined against SEC with 0 accepted identity resolutions. No labelled gold set: precision/recall unmeasured.

engines.name: CalFresh decision-registry acquirer (cap-aware slicing, sharded custody)
engines.one_line: Walk the California DSS decision registry (acms.dss.ca.gov, public, CAPTCHA parameter bypass value used by the site) by date slices, recursively halving any slice that returns the 100-row source cap down to single days; shard documents by SHA-256(document identity) mod 64; curl each PDF with retries, record headers/body hashes and magic-byte checks per attempt; reconcile to a registry denominator; archive per shard.
engines.coupling_notes: Each script bakes in an execution id, issue number, PARENT_MAIN commit, a GitHub Actions proof-artifact id/sha and a draft GitHub release tag. The registry-enumeration step that discovered the cap (423 partition requests, 212 terminal slices) comes from an external proof artifact and is NOT in the repo; querySlice() in shn-full-shard.mjs and shn-semantics.mjs is the only recursive-bisection code.

tests.status: pass (validate recorded results; no live network test)

engines.lift_out: Extract querySlice + shardForDocument + the per-attempt receipt shape into a ~200-line generic "capped-API slicer"; ignore the rest. 1-2 days. Registry content is a CDSS public record; check terms before bulk re-crawling.

patterns.what: Eleven non-negotiable invariants: no edge without receipt; hop = bounded surface only; temporal honesty; canonical controls identity; narration adds no facts; no identity-adjacent aggregation; density discipline; verification over trust; tool must not become capture; selection-layer neutrality (checked-in selection declaration, adjacent-actor symmetry, private leads cannot count as public coverage); interpretation contract travels with the data (denominator is not evidence, adversarial review by a second party).
patterns.maturity: high; copy verbatim and swap the case
patterns.enforcement: 1.1-1.4, 1.7, 1.8 by validate-release; 1.10/1.11 by validate:selection and validate:consumption; 1.5 by the narration test; 1.6 and 1.9 have no mechanical gate that I could find.
patterns.caveat: sections 2-8 are 2026-2037 roadmap and project-specific; section 8 amendment rule is a good governance clause.

patterns.what: Glossary: actor, organization, case anchor, bounded surface, hop basis, hop, path, claim, receipt, evidence class, validity window, temporal precision, undated participation, rejected hop pair, hop-eligible, scorable non-hop surface.

What creates a hop, source-of-truth pipeline (ledgers -> disposable build), temporal rule, receipt boundary statements (a listing proves a name appeared; registration is not attendance; absence from corpus means undocumented), density discipline, publication behaviour.

Claim status enum, causal_status enum, amount_kind enum (never "spent"), beacons are not guilt scores, structured report != approved publication, waterline = highest demonstrated publication transition.

harvest/triage/publish separation: observation -> candidate -> model/human draft -> deterministic review gate -> human-reviewed canonical change; ids from (source, official id) and content hash; hard identifiers drive joins, names are hints; amounts carry stage; promotion firewall.
Narrator adds no facts; optional human `plain` block with receipt_ids; machine-derived fallback must be labelled; a test fails when an anchor-adjacent actor lacks a receipt-backed profile.

Checked-in selection declaration per lane, symmetric comparison, coverage baseline, private-lead firewall; exported rows carry a machine-checked what-it-is/what-it-is-not statement; "neutral universe cleared" requires second-party adversarial review.
External review is a claim-specific evidence state, not a project gate: no external receipt -> record zero, keep the authority ceiling, continue unrelated lanes; outreach off by default.
Public-role-only scope; excluded categories; listing caveat.
How to prove two implementations produce identical ids (shared byte-identical vector file, hash checked before outputs, .gitattributes to stop line-ending drift); legacy token compatibility rule.
LEGACY edge shape for graph.json (evidence classes confirmed|primary_public|reported|derived|judgment|open; status vocabulary). Superseded by the surface/participation/receipt ledger.
patterns.caveat: There is NO JSON Schema for the current core model (surfaces, participation, receipts, claims, chains): schemas/ holds 127 files, 118 of them wave-specific (79 status-sovereignty, 39 counter-selector), 9 general (reporter-briefing, 5 poof-*, allocator-war, dca-field-record, k0-ceiling-conversion-event). The ledger shape lives only in code and data. docs/README.md also links a non-existent docs/evidence-model.md (3 times).

patterns.what: Newsroom-facing process objects: right-of-reply, referral packet, publication audit receipt, comprehension receipt with fixtures.
Pattern recognition is a discovery instrument not a verdict; operating procedure for research-track harness with cheap retrieval tier vs reasoning tier (validated on opportunity-zones runs).

patterns.what: Convention that every machine-produced object declares what it is NOT allowed to do; 233 of 386 validators assert it.
patterns.maturity: high idea, over-applied (it is the main source of validator boilerplate)

patterns.what: Technique: when a registry caps responses (100), split the date interval recursively until under the cap or a single day; flag unresolved caps; shard documents by SHA-256 mod N for content-neutral parallelism; per-attempt receipts with headers hash, body hash and magic-byte check.

validator_breakdown.method: Static analysis of each tools/validate-* file plus one level of its imports (./build-*, ./lib/*): which paths it reads (data/intake, receipts, workflows, package.json, docs, git), whether it opens/hashes raw captured bytes, whether it recomputes its sibling builder, pins hashes/SHAs; then manual sampling of 2-4 validators per family (counter-selector-20, k0-05, m05 intel custody amendment, rd04 state-source adjudication, fec-oppexp-cohort, oge-beneficial-interests, natsec100 roster-recovery, schoolhouse irs filing-index, preference v30). Heuristic: treat bucket edges as +-5 points.

abstract_spec_self_validation.what: preference-custody v9-v59 and preference-linkage-* "laboratory floor" chain. Each validator loads a build produced by the sibling compile-preference-* script from tools/lib/preference-*.mjs and re-derives it from the same lib plus a synthetic fixture. Zero real-world input; every docs page says it "creates no real-world finding".

research_ledger_adjudication_consistency.what: m05 (53), status-sovereignty (non-capture; ~48), k0 (17), a few lane manifests. They load hand-authored JSON about real-world topics and assert counts/denominators/enums/graph_effect:none/pinned SHA-256 of the authored files and of predecessor validators (git blob SHAs). They verify that the project's own records did not drift; they do not re-open the captured source bytes.

repo_process_wave_chain_wiring.what: counter-selector waves (38+1: wave_id, as_of, parent_main_sha, parent_release_sha256, registries), project-stable-ground checkpoints (12), estate/gametrail/aperture/report page projections (12), m04d-g (5), and release/pages/poof/security-state gates (21). Many shell out to git (diff/changed-path surface), read .github/workflows, or pin parent commits.

real_world_data_checks.what: Schoolhouse custody (12), OGE/FEC/disclosure/NatSec100/gov-property/officeholder/portfolio lanes (14), electric-twin (3), and ssc validators that touch captured pages (27). Mostly manifest reconciliation (sums of per-person counts == totals, denominators, hash format) against data/research manifests or sealed zips.

validator_breakdown.validate_release_internals: tools/validate-release.mjs is 2,152 lines. Generic constitutional checks (ledger integrity, density, every hop carries its surface basis, rejected pairs genuinely disjoint, recompute AXM identity layer, receipt archival gate, no session-local paths) are roughly lines 57-232 and 1482-1538 and 1875-1895 (~20%). The remaining ~1,700 lines are hard-coded regression fixtures for specific UK/US actors (Ben Warner, Electric Twin, Anduril UK, Simon Case, Detachment 201, Faculty...). The generic part is the reusable part.
validator_breakdown.line_footprint_note: All 386 validators = 48,271 lines; the 119 preference validators are small (2.3k lines) because the weight is in tools/lib/preference-* (52k lines).

tests.how_run: Copied the repo (minus .git, dist, node_modules; node_modules symlinked) into the scratchpad, git-init-ed the copy, and ran each test file with plain `node <file>` (60-180s timeout each). First pass: the 111 files listed in `npm test`, 6 in parallel (2 failed from a build/ write race and passed when re-run serially). Second pass: every test/*.test.js serially. The original repo was not written to by this audit (git status clean); note HEAD moved during the audit because other agents committed retrospective/ (3 commits) on top of d8392cfb.
tests.note_unwired: Only ~24% of test files are in `npm test`; the rest (preference-*, counter-selector-*, m05-*, k0-*, ssc-*, schoolhouse, etc.) are reachable only from per-wave GitHub workflows.
tests.summary: Of 471 test files run, 458 pass. 13 fail: 2 are genuine repo defects, 10 are environment-only (root guard x2, no Chromium x1, shallow git history x7), 1 is a 150 s timeout of the recursive preference chain (v59). All 111 files in `npm test` pass.

genuine_failures_in_original_repo.cause: asserts exactly 1 non-hop directory_roster_surface in data/ledger/surfaces.jsonl; the ledger now has 7 (stale assertion). Not in npm test so CI misses it. Reproduced on a clean copy.

tools/validate-m05-...-cross-domain-source-custody-correction.mjs pins the git blob SHA of test/m05-source-health-evidence-state-regression.test.js (matches) AND requires that file to contain the strings missing-source-locator / foreign-source-host / promotedOfficialContract (it does not contain missing-source-locator). Internally inconsistent validator; reproduced by running the validator directly in the original repo.

environment_only_failures.cause: Playwright cannot launch: no Chromium in this sandbox (/opt/pw-browsers missing). Other *-browser tests, if any remain unrun, fail the same way.
refuses to run as root ("descriptor-relative receipt helper may not run as root"); sandbox runs as root. Not verified as non-root. test/industrial-exhaust.test.js (feed layer) passes.
